gaps.sentence: 'Leave now or I'll call the police!' he shouted. He ___ to call the police.
gaps.explanation: A threatening conditional utterance is reported as threatened to do something.

gaps.sentence: He ___ me his car for the weekend.
gaps.explanation: Offer takes the double-object pattern (offer somebody something); the others do not.

gaps.sentence: 'I didn't take your charger,' she insisted. She ___ taking my charger.
gaps.explanation: Denials are reported as deny + -ing: denied taking.

gaps.sentence: 'Leave the building immediately!' the firefighter ordered. The firefighter ordered us ___ the building immediately.
gaps.explanation: Orders are reported with order + object + to-infinitive.

gaps.sentence: 'I might take a gap year,' he said. He said he ___ take a gap year.
gaps.explanation: Might has no further backshift form; it stays might.

gaps.sentence: 'I used to live in Cairo,' she mentioned. She mentioned that she ___ to live in Cairo.
gaps.explanation: 'Used to' has no backshift form; it remains used to after a past reporting verb.

gaps.sentence: 'Come round to my house tomorrow,' she said. She invited me round to her house ___.
gaps.explanation: Tomorrow becomes the next day (the following day) when the invitation is reported.

gaps.sentence: 'The road is being resurfaced,' the council said. The council said the road ___ resurfaced.
gaps.explanation: Present continuous passive (is being resurfaced) backshifts to past continuous passive: was being resurfaced.
